title: The Rate at Which a Certificate Is Re-Rated
content:
The rate at which a certificate of the Travel Protection Plans is re-rated is read off the shape of the
policy's own premium record: which kinds of line the premium was originally built from.

## The three readings

1. Where the premium record carries an age loading line and a destination loading line, the rate applied is the
   one the premium collected bears to the trip cost the base premium line was rated on.
2. Where the premium record carries a base premium line and no age loading line, the rate applied is the plan's
   base rate alone.
3. In every other case the rate applied is the plan's base rate as a proportion of the declared trip cost,
   increased by the plan's destination loading percentage of that base rate.

The trip cost the base premium line was rated on, named in the first reading, is the base premium standing
collected on the record divided by the plan's base rate taken as a proportion; and the premium collected, in
that same reading, is the premium the record shows collected on the policy.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A policy on a plan whose base rate is 6.8 per cent carries a base premium line of 476.00, an age loading line
and a destination loading line, and shows 680.00 collected in all. The trip cost the base premium line was rated
on is 7000.00, and the rate applied is the one 680.00 bears to 7000.00, which is 9.71 per cent and not any
figure the plan's schedule carries. On the same policy carrying a base premium line and no age loading line, the
rate applied under the second reading would be the plan's base rate alone, 6.8 per cent. On a policy carrying an
age loading line but no destination loading line, neither of the first two readings holds, and the third answers.
The figures are hypothetical.
